# About the MTM

MTM (Media Technology Monitor) is a continuous, bilingual research initiative that tracks how Canadians use media and technology — from streaming and social platforms to devices and emerging tech — across English and French Canada. Running since 2005, MTM exists so that understanding how Canadians actually use media doesn't require guesswork: broadcasters, advertisers, educators, and policymakers all plan around the same independent numbers.

## What makes the data reliable

Scale

12,000+ Canadians surveyed twice a year — enough sample to break down by niche demographics.

Recency

Refreshed every spring and fall, so the numbers reflect how Canadians use media right now.

Coverage

5,000+ variables across demographics, devices, and platforms — one dataset, not a patchwork of surveys.

Comparability

The same core methodology every wave since 2005, so trend claims actually hold up.

## Timeline

Every wave since 2005 uses the same core methodology, so a claim about how Canadian media habits shifted can be traced to an exact year.

1. 2005

   MTM launches

   An annual fall survey of 8,000 Canadians, gathering media and technology data by landline telephone.

2. 2010

   Spring wave added

   The annual sample grows to 12,000 Canadians across fall and spring waves — the release cadence still used today.

3. 2011

   MTM Portal launches

   MTM data becomes available online for the first time, giving users direct access to survey findings.

4. 2012

   Cell-phone-only households added

   The sample is updated to keep pace with how Canadians were actually reachable by phone, as landlines gave way to mobile.

5. 2015

   10th anniversary

   The interactive Trending Tool and Forecasting Tool launch, unlocking 1,500+ data points for exploration.

6. 2019

   MTM Jr. launches

   Coverage extends to Canadians aged 2–17, with additional EDI questions added to the survey.

7. 2021

   MTM Newcomers launches

   A dedicated survey reaches Canadians new to the country, while the sample also expands to include Northern Canada and a booster sample of Indigenous respondents.

8. 2022

   MTM Jr. sample grows

   The MTM Jr. sample expands, sharpening the picture of media habits among younger Canadians.

9. 2023

   70+ reports released

   Data from across the year turns into reports and infographics, making insights easier to share and act on.

10. 2024

    YourData tool launches

    Users can create high quality, report ready tables and charts themselves directly on the Portal.

11. 2025

    MTM Census Tool launches

    Census data becomes directly explorable within the Portal.

12. 2026

    Census Tool 2.0 & AskMTM

    An upgraded Census Tool arrives alongside a new AI chatbot, making it faster to find answers within MTM's data.

13. Today

    [Reach out to us today!](https://aishwaryabhattbhatt-cbc.github.io/mtm-website-4/en/request-demo/)
